title: Optimizing Parameters for High Resolution Near Axis Transmission Kikuchi Diffraction
content: It has been over a decade since Keller & Geiss [1] obtained 10nm resolution with Electron Backscatter Diffraction (EBSD) by using diffraction patterns from electron transmission instead of more conventional geometry. More recent developments in non-conventional geometry for Transmission Kikuchi Diffraction (TKD) have added to the number of parameters that need to be optimized to obtain spatial resolutions of 2nm at meaningful speeds. Previous TKD investigations have recorded the effect of atomic number, sample tilt angle, accelerating voltage and sample thickness on spatial resolution [2]. Sample thickness and sample preparation remain the dominant factors determining spatial resolution for conventional TKD; however, the parameters mentioned above require further investigation as non-conventional TKD geometries emerge.
